Someone contacted me to work on their project. I'm not currently a professional programmer, but I have taught myself how to program. What rate should I charge, and what are some general guidelines I should establish for the project?

Thanks.
I can't really offer advice on what you asked, but absolutely get everything on paper! Freelancers get screwed so often so having records is imperative.

Entirely depends on what your time is worth to you, and how good of a job you think you can do. Make sure she knows that you don't promise your customer long term support, but you're happy to help out if you can.

I work on retainer. Kind of like a lawyer would. It's $5,000 upfront. Non-refundable. Use-it-or-lose-it.

I generally get a no-frills extremely rough prototype up for free. (After the retainer is paid)

Then we define the spec of the project and divide it up until each piece can no longer be subdivided. I charge $100 (Taken out of the retainer) for each piece. If the piece is trivial enough that it's not worth $100 I recommend hiring an student from the local community college to do it. (For instance, proof reading).

If the piece seems trivial, but the client can't find an intern capable of doing it, then I tell them, "Well, the piece isn't so trivial after all, is it?"

This way, I'm getting compensated for the things at my level. The client has incentive to get as much out of what he paid for. But, at the same time, I'm not bogged down with less important stuff.

If the spec is changed on an already written module, there isn't any "Can you just go in and tweak this one teensy little thing? (For free)". That's considered a new spec and it's either $100 or hire an intern.

Also, the project has a clear deadline, when the $5,000 is dry the project is clearly done. If more features need to be added it's another $5,000.
